rationale: Block 3 defines osteoporosis and its diagnostic threshold — the T-score cut-off is a foundational fact students must recall exactly to avoid under- or over-diagnosing osteoporosis on DEXA.
Block 4 covers osteomalacia — its characteristic pseudofractures (Looser's zones) and the biochemical pattern (low Ca/PO4, raised ALP, raised PTH) are high-yield discriminators vs osteoporosis.

Block 10 covers Paget's disease clinical features and investigations — the characteristic markedly raised ALP with normal serum calcium is a classic exam trap that distinguishes Paget's from hyperparathyroidism and malignancy.

Block 15 covers rickets deformity management — the key principle that surgical correction (osteotomy) must be deferred until the metabolic disease is fully corrected and the child reaches skeletal maturity is a common exam trap.
